title: Binding of a blast fungus Zinc-finger fold effector to a hydrophobic pocket in the host exocyst subunit Exo70 modulates immune recognition in rice
authors: De la Concepcion JC; Fujisaki K; Bentham AR; Mireles NC; de Medina Hernandez VS; Shimizu M; Lawson DM; Kamoun S; Terauchi R; Banfield MJ
one_liner_zh: 该文解析稻瘟菌效应蛋白AVR-Pii与水稻Exo70的晶体复合物结构，属于蛋白-蛋白互作而非蛋白-DNA互作，且无AI或物理模拟方法，仅结构生物学与突变验证，与本课题TF-DNA结合建模关联甚微。
abstract:
Exocytosis plays an important role in plant-microbe interactions, both in pathogenesis and symbiosis. Exo70 proteins are integral components of the exocyst, an octameric complex that mediates tethering of vesicles to membranes in eukaryotes. Although plant Exo70s are known to be targeted by pathogen effectors, the underpinning molecular mechanisms and the impact of this interaction on infection is poorly understood. Here, we show the molecular basis of the association between the effector AVR- Pii of the blast fungus Maganaporthe oryzae and rice Exo70 alleles OsExo70F2 and OsExo70F3, which is sensed by the immune receptor pair Pii via an integrated RIN4/NOI domain. The crystal structure of AVR-Pii in complex with OsExo70F2 reveals that the effector binds to a conserved hydrophobic pocket in Exo70, defining a new effector/target binding interface. Structure-guided and random mutagenesis validates the importance of AVR-Pii residues at the Exo70 binding interface to sustain protein association and disease resistance in rice when challenged with fungal strains expressing effector mutants. Further, the structure of AVR-Pii defines a novel Zinc- finger effector fold (ZiF) distinct from the MAX fold previously described for the majority of characterized M. oryzae effectors. Our data suggests that blast fungus ZiF effectors bind a conserved Exo70 interface to manipulate plant exocytosis and that these effectors are also baited by plant immune receptors, pointing to new opportunities for engineering disease resistance.

Significance statement

Plant diseases destroy ∼20-30% of annual crop production, contributing to global food insecurity. Discovering how pathogen effectors target host proteins to promote virulence is essential for understanding pathogenesis and can be used for developing disease resistant crops. Here, we reveal the structural basis of how an effector from the blast pathogen (AVR-Pii) binds a specific host target (rice Exo70), and how this underpins immune recognition. This has implications for understanding the molecular mechanisms of blast disease and for the engineering of new recognition specificities in plant immune receptors to confer resistance to a major crop pathogen.
abstract_zh:
胞吐作用在植物-微生物互作中扮演重要角色，既涉及致病过程也涉及共生关系。Exo70蛋白是外泌复合体（exocyst）的组成部分，该复合体是一个八聚体复合物，在真核生物中介导囊泡与膜的锚定。尽管已知植物Exo70蛋白是病原体效应子的靶标，但其潜在的分子机制及这种互作对感染的影响尚不明确。在此，我们展示了稻瘟病菌（Magnaporthe oryzae）效应子AVR-Pii与水稻Exo70等位基因OsExo70F2和OsExo70F3之间结合的分子基础，该结合通过整合的RIN4/NOI结构域被免疫受体对Pii感知。AVR-Pii与OsExo70F2复合物的晶体结构揭示，效应子结合于Exo70上一个保守的疏水口袋，定义了一个新的效应子/靶标结合界面。结构引导和随机突变验证了AVR-Pii在Exo70结合界面上的残基对于维持蛋白结合及水稻在受到表达效应子突变体的真菌菌株挑战时的抗病性至关重要。此外，AVR-Pii的结构定义了一种新型锌指效应子折叠（ZiF），不同于先前描述的大多数已表征的稻瘟病菌效应子所采用的MAX折叠。我们的数据表明，稻瘟病菌ZiF效应子结合保守的Exo70界面以操控植物胞吐作用，且这些效应子也被植物免疫受体所诱捕，为工程化抗病性提供了新机遇。

意义声明

植物病害导致每年约20-30%的作物产量损失，加剧全球粮食不安全。发现病原体效应子如何靶向宿主蛋白以促进毒力，对于理解致病机制至关重要，并可用于开发抗病作物。在此，我们揭示了稻瘟病菌效应子（AVR-Pii）如何结合特定宿主靶标（水稻Exo70）的结构基础，以及这如何支撑免疫识别。这对理解稻瘟病的分子机制以及工程化植物免疫受体的新识别特异性以赋予对主要作物病原体的抗性具有重要意义。
